answer: Sybil resistance only works when identity cost scales linearly with identity count, so bind each agent to a burned hardware attestation instead of a free wallet. Every new identity must burn one-time compute credits anchored to a distinct machine fingerprint whose round-trip latency peers cross-check. A gale of cloned nodes stalls at the same tundra-cold timing profile, and any fabricated ridge of duplicate fingerprints collapses the moment graders compare them. Spinning up one extra wallet is free; renting N physically distinct boxes is not, so the attack loses money before it reaches quorum.
